frozen_original.title: Bondi DOJ Refuses to Enforce Campaign Finance Laws Against Trump Allies
frozen_original.synopsis: By April 2025, it had become clear that the DOJ's campaign finance enforcement division had effectively ceased pursuing cases against Trump allies and affiliated PACs, despite documented violations brought to the department's attention by career prosecutors and the FEC. Cases involving dark money flows, straw donor schemes, and foreign contribution violations connected to Trump political organizations were shelved or closed without explanation. The non-enforcement of campaign finance law against one political party while formally maintaining the laws on the books represented a selective nullification of election law — a form of institutional corruption that undermined the legal equality that democratic elections require.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Ends Section 8 Housing Voucher Program for New Applicants
proposal.original_synopsis: In April 2025, the Trump administration announced it would not fund new Housing Choice Vouchers — the Section 8 program that subsidized housing costs for over 2 million extremely low-income families, seniors, and disabled people — while simultaneously proposing deep cuts to rental assistance funding in the Big Beautiful Bill. New applicants who had waited years on housing authority waiting lists were removed from consideration. Existing voucher holders faced uncertainty as funding reductions threatened to force housing authorities to rescind vouchers already in use. Housing advocates warned the cuts would fuel increases in homelessness, particularly among elderly and disabled Americans who had been on waiting lists for years. The elimination of new vouchers was projected to leave tens of thousands of additional families in unaffordable housing situations with no federal remedy.
